claims.claim: the official overview describes it as covering address book, cloud documents, messaging, meetings, calendars, smart documents, and other common enterprise scenarios with over one thousand standardized interfaces.
claims.summary: The official WPS open-platform overview (guide/overview.md) states WPS 365 capabilities are registered as open interfaces and the platform provides over one thousand standardized interfaces covering contacts, cloud documents, messaging, meetings, calendars, smart documents, and other common enterprise scenarios.

claims.claim: The client connects directly to the official production host `https://openapi.wps.cn` (path prefix `/v7`) with the caller's own OAuth2 credentials.
claims.summary: Official WPS 365 Endpoint documentation (e.g. list-installed-apps) shows request addresses on https://openapi.wps.cn/v7/..., and the certification guide describes the access_token (OAuth2) authentication mechanism for every call.

claims.claim: Create an application on the open.wps.cn developer console and apply for the permission scopes each workflow needs.
claims.summary: The official WPS open-platform overview describes the developer console application model and the application permission system (应用权限体系) that binds interface-call permissions to applications.

claims.claim: The official authorization model has two token classes: the app (application) authorization token for resources owned by the application, and the delegated (user) authorization token when acting on behalf of a specific user.
claims.summary: The official certification-authorization summary defines two access-token classes: user authorization tokens (delegated) and application authorization tokens (app), with different resource scope per class.

claims.claim: KSO-1 request signing is optional and enabled per application under the developer console security settings.
claims.summary: The official KSO-1 signature algorithm document states KSO-1 signing only applies when the developer console security setting for interface signing is enabled.

claims.claim: requests must carry the `X-Kso-Date` and `X-Kso-Authorization` headers with an HMAC-SHA256 signature
claims.summary: The official KSO-1 signature algorithm document specifies the X-Kso-Date and X-Kso-Authorization headers and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over method, URI, content type, date, and request-body hash.

claims.claim: Streaming Endpoints under `/v7/sse/*` (AI docs search, document QA, AIPPT generation, agent chat), plus two AIPPT variants under `/v7/aippt/*` (`gen_slides_from_multipages` and `generate_slides_from_pxf_v2`), return `text/event-stream` responses.
claims.summary: The official OpenAPI document declares text/event-stream 200 responses for /v7/sse/* operations (aidocs, docqa, aippt, generator, wps365agent) and the /v7/aippt/gen_slides_from_multipages and /v7/aippt/generate_slides_from_pxf_v2 variants; the official AIPPT docs describe the SSE streaming flow.

claims.claim: The machine contract enumerates no per-Endpoint event names: every event is a JSON payload that carries the type and terminal-state markers.
claims.summary: The official OpenAPI document declares no SSE event names for these Endpoints; the AIPPT docs show in-payload stream_status/type terminal markers (e.g. stream_status=done, type=generate_pptx_finish).

claims.claim: each event carries `encrypted_data`, `signature`, `nonce`, `topic`, `operation`, and `time` fields. The `nonce` field is the IV vector for AES-CBC decryption; verify the HMAC-SHA256 `signature` over `access_key:topic:nonce:time:encrypted_data` before processing.
claims.summary: The official event security-verification document defines the encrypted event body fields (encrypted_data, signature, nonce, topic, operation, time), states nonce is the IV vector for AES-CBC decryption, and defines the HMAC-SHA256 signature over access_key:topic:nonce:time:encrypted_data.
